segments.text: The rule of law is the principle that all people are equal before the law and that no power
holder may stand above the law.
This principle, which began in ancient Rome, forms the foundation of modern democratic society
A constitution stands as the supreme law, and every other law is placed beneath it in the real world
However, there are many countries where the rule of law does not work well enough
Corruption spreads and those in power sometimes twist the law to their own advantage
Judges may come under political pressure and lose the ability to make independent decisions
A person who commits a crime is brought to trial and if found guilty is confined
But in recent years the purpose of punishment has been shifting from mere penalty toward rehabilitation
The aim is to help former prisoners return to society
And to prevent them from falling back into criminal conduct
Citizens to carry the responsibility of taking part
In upholding the law
When citizens raise their voices against wrongdoing
And demand transparency of the system
They support the health of democratic society
Law is the promise of a society
The will to keep that promise and to reform it as needed
Is what builds the foundation of a free and just society
You
